events.name: Deep in the Sounds
events.summary: Three days deep in the outer Sounds — promoted on Facebook alongside Nelson Motorcycles. Details and entries direct with Dave.
body: The ride

A multi-day run into the outer Marlborough Sounds, announced through the Kohatu and Nelson Motorcycles riding network on Facebook. Route, accommodation and entry details are handled directly by Dave — get in touch fast, because Sounds rides fill on word of mouth alone.

events.name: The Five Year Plan
events.dateLabel: August 2026 · exact dates to be confirmed
events.distance: The length of New Zealand over five years
events.summary: Ride the length of New Zealand over five years, starting at Cape Reinga. Six days a year of off-road tracks, private land and scenic trails — with a prizegiving on Stewart Island for every rider who completes the journey.
timeline: Lower South Island — prizegiving on Stewart Island
body: The plan

Starting at Cape Reinga, this is a five-year journey riding the length of New Zealand — off-road tracks, private land and scenic public trails, with rest days between weeks of riding. Join a single year's leg, or challenge yourself and ride the whole length: each year starts from Cape Reinga, so in year five you can choose one week in the deep south or five weeks top to bottom.
Good to know
The final Year 1 itinerary and rider information pack will be issued once dates and route permissions are confirmed.

GPS or phone mount for the supplied GPX route

events.name: Sounds Like
events.summary: Two days on private farm tracks and gravel across three big outer-Sounds farms including Te Kuta and Port Ligar, overnighting at the French Pass hall.
body: The ride

Two full days on private farm tracks and gravel in and around Marlborough's Admiralty Bay and French Pass. The off-road runs across three large outer-Sounds farms including Te Kuta and Port Ligar — country you can't reach any other way, with the Sounds below you most of the day.
The overnight

We stay at the French Pass hall, and the event fundraises to support the community that hosts us — dinner and breakfast are included. Bring a mattress and sleeping bag; they travel in the support vehicle.
bring: Road-registered adventure bike with current registration and WoF
GPS loaded with the supplied GPX route

events.name: The Clarence
events.summary: Private stations the whole way — Tempello, the Clarence Valley and Muzzle, then Glenhope — with a tractor river crossing if the water's up, shearers' quarters hospitality and a night in Hanmer.
itinerary: Over the Maungatapu to Blenheim, then into Tempello Station to reach the Awatere Valley and cross the Awatere River (conditions allowing). South to Kekerengu, where the local community hosts us for the night — dinner and breakfast included, bunking down in the shearers' quarters or on mats in the hall.
Day 2 — The Clarence Valley to Hanmer

South through three private stations in the Clarence Valley. We cross the Clarence River — by tractor if the water's up — exit through Muzzle Station and Blind Saddle onto the Inland Kaikoura Road, then over another private farm across the St James Range into Hanmer Springs. Accommodation included.

Out on the Lewis Pass road and into Glenhope Station for 55 km of backcountry tracks with a lunch stop provided. Exit at Boyle Village and cruise home via Maruia Saddle, Murchison, Braeburn and Porika.
body: The ride

Three full days on a mixture of road, private farm tracks and gravel through country you simply cannot ride any other way — the Awatere, the Clarence Valley's remote stations, and the St James country into Hanmer. Entries feed directly back into the districts we ride through.
Is this for me?

Grade 3 — Station rider. You should be comfortable standing on the pegs for long stretches, riding rutted farm climbs and crossing rivers. It's a big-distance ride, not a technical enduro — but weather can turn farm track into hard work fast. Adventure-oriented off-road tyres are a must, and your bike needs a fuel range of 250 km+ between stops.
included: Dinner & breakfast at Kekerengu, lunch day 3
bring: Road-registered adventure bike with current registration and WoF
GPS loaded with the supplied GPX route
faqs: What happens if weather closes a section?
Routes cross live rivers and working stations, so sections can change on the day. We scout ahead, and sweep riders carry comms — if a crossing isn't safe, there's always a plan B.
Do I need any special licence or paperwork?
A current motorcycle licence and a road-legal bike (registration + WoF) — much of the route links public roads between the private sections. You'll sign a land-access waiver at sign-on.

events.name: Nelson Tasman Motorcycle Festival
events.summary: Adventure bikes ride private-land courses both days; road bikes join a Saturday treasure hunt — then everyone rolls into Founders Heritage Park for vendors, food trucks and displays. Raising funds for Nelson Tasman Search & Rescue.
films: Nelson Tasman Motorcycle Festival 2025 — full film
body: Adventure programme
Adventure bikes ride private-land courses on both days. Entry NZ$350 — suitable off-road-capable adventure bikes; grading and requirements confirmed with the entry pack.
Road-bike programme
Road bikes of every class join the Saturday treasure hunt around Nelson Tasman. Entry NZ$45 — open to all road-registered bikes.
The finish
Everyone rolls into Founders Heritage Park together — static displays, vendors and food trucks, open to the public. The festival raises funds for Nelson Tasman Search & Rescue.

events.name: Wellington Motorcycle Festival
events.summary: Adventure courses over council parks, forestry and private land not normally open to riders, plus a Saturday poker run from Trentham and Masterton to Brewtown.
body: Adventure programme
Adventure courses run over two days across council parks, forestry and private land not normally open to riders. Entry NZ$350.
Road-bike programme
Saturday's poker run starts in Trentham and Masterton and ends at Brewtown — seven locations, collect a card at each, best poker hand wins. Entry NZ$45.
The evening
Saturday evening, all riders gather at the Brewtown greenspace for static displays while the brews and food trucks keep everyone fed.

events.name: Lake Matiri — with a tractor
events.summary: A 237 km day starting in Nelson, with a genuine party trick at Mt Ella Station — a tractor river crossing — before lunch in Murchison and the run into the Matiri. Sold out.
body: The ride

A 237 km day starting in Nelson, with a genuine party trick at Mt Ella Station — bikes towed across the river by tractor if you wanted to keep your feet dry — before lunch in Murchison and the run through DOC and power-station land into the Matiri Valley. The ride sold out.

events.name: Anything Mechanical
events.summary: Registration at Nelson Motorcycles, farm tracks through the Dicks and Parkes farms, a climb to the Inwoods Lookout at around 1,000 m, then three hours exploring 55 km of tracks at the Anything Mechanical farm.
body: The ride

Registration and briefing at Nelson Motorcycles, then out through Brightwater into farm tracks on the Dicks and Parkes farms — including a tricky mud climb where good tyres earned their keep. A climb to the Inwoods Lookout at around 1,000 m, a short road link, then three hours exploring 55 km of tracks at the Anything Mechanical farm. Sign-out at the Sprig & Fern, Brightwater. NZ$20 of every entry went to farm track maintenance.

body: The ride

events.name: Trail Ride Round 1 — Anything Mechanical, St Arnaud
events.summary: A full day for trail and enduro bikes without rego — private farmland, forest and back-country trails near St Arnaud, open for one day only. Marshals, recovery and first aid on site.
body: The ride

A full day through private farmland, forest and back-country trails near the Top of the South, for non-road-registered trail and enduro bikes. Sign-on from 7:30am, riders' briefing 8:15am, start 8:30am, finish 3pm. A main loop for competent off-road riders, optional technical sections for the hungry, and marshals, recovery and first aid on site all day.
